claims.statement: app-lynx is the repository's only runtime client; the SolidJS + Capacitor webview client (packages/app) was deleted in ADR-0203, with its Android host moved to packages/android-host and its OAuth credentials/version facts moved to app-lynx.

All list feed pages (IllustList/NovelList/Following/UserHome/Bookmarks) and the discover carousel converge on the createMixFeed deep module for pagination; pages are thin ref-snapshot bridges (sync) that dispose-and-rebuild the feed instance on tab/mode switches rather than mutating state.

createMixFeed hides double debounce (800ms throttle + 3s cooldown), generation-gate plus AbortController race protection, cross-source dedupe, pageSize=20 batch rendering, a 15s timeout, and separate firstError/pageError error slots; a one-shot retry timer re-fires debounce-swallowed scrolltolower events and notifies the page through onUpdate.

createMixFeed supports two merge modes — ratio (default [4,1] alternation) and time-merge (global create_date descending interleave); the discover page uses time-merge while other list pages use the default ratio.

The discover page renders the mixed feed as a hand-rolled single-card swipe carousel whose background-thread touch handlers drive an offset applied via marginLeft (not transform: translateX, whose translated container fails to render its children on device), fed by a createMixFeed instance rebuilt per in-page all/illust/novel tab with merge: 'time-merge'; it has an infinite slide stream, render-layer filtering of restricted/AI/tag-muted items while the data layer still loads them (so toggling settings recomputes without re-fetching), and a refreshEpoch remount that returns to the first slide.

Native lynx <list> mis-handles structural in-place patches (mid-list insert silently dropped, single remove leaves a hole, whole replace misaligns), so list pages bump a refreshEpoch and bind it as <list :key> to force whole-tree rebuild; back-to-top is also implemented as rebuild because no JS scroll-to-offset API exists.

R18/R18G content is account-scoped via show_r18_${uid} and show_r18g_${uid} with a pure isRestricted predicate; lists render the full item under a restricted card/overlay instead of filtering it out, so toggling the switch unmasks instantly without a re-fetch.

AI content uses the account-scoped ai_filter_mode_${uid} three-state setting; isAiWork is ai_type >= 1, mask renders AI restricted cards, and only is the sole AI state that removes items at the data layer (dropping non-AI works).

Tag mute is account-scoped mute_tags_${uid}, an exact tag.name.trim() set membership test with no normalization or translated_name matching; it is applied as data-layer removal (mute equals invisible, not masked), reads a non-reactive snapshot to avoid native list mid-remove, and in ranking it assigns rank first then drops muted entries leaving rank holes.

Global search is a bottom-sheet command palette backed by the useSearch state machine: 300ms input debounce, AbortController rotation with last-write-wins race handling, scope=all parallel illust+novel requests merged by create_date, and dual-cursor pagination that keeps loaded results and sets a paginationError slot on page failure.

Search filter state and request construction are single-sourced in the zero-IO @pictelio/search-core package: SearchFilters spans period/bookmark/ratio/minPixels/aiOverride, and buildIllustSearchRequest/buildNovelSearchRequest, normalizeFilters, buildCacheKey, resolveAiMode, and filterByBookmarkBand all derive from that canonical state.

popular_desc routes search to popular-preview endpoints with no sort, pagination, or bookmark band; search_target differs by class (single-word illust queries omit it, novels always send partial/exact_match_for_tags); the bookmark band is applied as a client-side fallback on non-popular paths and dropped on the popular path.

Ranking is single-sourced in @pictelio/ranking-core (7 RANK_MODES with id/apiMode pairs, buildRankingRequest for /v1/illust/ranking, rankingCacheKey normalizing today, and JST date helpers without Intl); rank is render-stream index + 1 with page order preserved, restricted items are masked with rank preserved, and muted items are dropped leaving rank holes.

Related-works injection uses a one-shot pendingAnchor plus a rowFor render query, and renders results as an inline expanding section inside the anchor card (RelatedInlineSection) because native waterfall lists silently drop mid-list insertions; rows are filtered by isRestricted, isAiRestricted, and isTagMuted.

Tag neighbors (ADR-0197) is an explainable in-Pixiv similar-works search with two phases: author-first (recent <=300 author works, local Jaccard >=30%, top 20) then global tag-combination relaxation stopping once a layer returns >=5 items; it uses raw tag.name only, never mixes in author names, and surfaces a visible count of gate-hidden items rather than silently filtering.

Search history is a device-level (not account-scoped) 10-item idbKV list written only at search commit points, and search pagination next_url is SSRF-guarded to the app-api.pixiv.net hostname before fetching.

Account-scoped content settings (R18, AI mode, mute tags) persist through the shared CapacitorStorage channel (PictelioPrefs native / idbKV web-core), and logout resets their in-memory values to defaults without writing.

Page-level first-load skeleton is driven by settle semantics — a source settles on success including zero items but not on failure — via deriveFirstLoadView and the createMixFeed settled() accessor, so existing data refreshes never flash the skeleton and only a settled-empty result shows the empty state.

The swipe carousel deliberately keeps its background-thread implementation because main-thread scripts are usable after all: the blank page previously blamed on main-thread bindings came from importing a helper module without the 'main thread' directive (helpers get stripped by the MT bundler), and MTS is now framed as a performance optimisation that would require inlining helpers while keeping marginLeft translation.

The discover carousel's title/author/tags/bookmark scrim is a single page-level overlay driven by the current slide index rather than one scrim per slide, and its text sits on a stable inverse-surface / inverse-on-surface background because the gradient alone measured only 1.56:1 (title) and 2.17:1 (author) contrast over cover pixels.

The four top-level destinations are a deliberately closed 4-item NAV_TABS array answering four different user questions (discover /discover, updates /updates, shelf /shelf, me /me), and the media axis was demoted to in-page tabs so /illusts and /novels keep their routes for deep links, benchNav and back targets while appearing in no navigation.

/updates is a three-section preview aggregate (following / watchlist / notifications) and /shelf a three-segment preview aggregate (bookmarks / watch later / continue reading), each rendering at most PREVIEW_N = 3 rows and linking into the owning secondary page; the sections load and fail independently, and each keeps its own loading flag so an unfinished hydrate is never rendered as an empty state.

Pagination ownership has two documented exceptions to the createMixFeed convergence: the watchlist's series-shaped items use their own createWatchlistFeed deep module with createMixFeed-equivalent semantics (series-id dedupe, generation gate, split error slots, one-shot in-flight retry and an explicit removeItem) but no AbortController pass-through, while FollowList's follow/follower list keeps hand-written cursor paging because ADR-0104 deliberately left it (and comment paging) outside createMixFeed.

In-row actions must sit at the row's leading edge because the GlobalFab's horizontal band permanently occupies the row tail: ADR-0221 moved four destructive actions (ContinueRow, Watchlist, WatchLater, MuteTags) to leading 40 dp round icon buttons that keep destructive semantics in the icon colour and add a press-state layer, requiring @tap.stop only on rows whose root also handles tap.

Native constraints shape list-row internals: lynx does not honour pointer-events, so a full-screen overlay must be v-if-gated with a tap handler or reduced to a zero-size anchor; a list-item root must be one stable view without conditional branches or event handlers, so taps bind on an inner view; and absolute positioning inside a list-item is banned because the engine counts it into content height, which is why AdaptiveTagRow renders all chips under overflow-hidden, measures them with selector-query bounding rects and re-renders, falling back to a fixed cap with a warning.

RefreshableList is the list scroll/operations container that owns the FAB menu state machine, the rotation animation and the app's only useScrollIndicator instance, exposes a scoped onScroll that pages must bind with scroll-event-throttle = 0, and emits back-to-top so the page rebuilds the list (the rebuild is the scroll-to-top); tab pages keep the container with fab = false and register refresh/backToTop on the global radial FAB via useGlobalFabStore().usePage(name).

FeedListFooter is the props-driven three-state list tail (loading / inline pagination error / end-of-feed) with an optional retry form that emits @retry, and pages keep the wrapping full-span list-item because native <list> only accepts list-item children.

Tag muting is triggered by a 500 ms long press bound at the view layer (TagPressChip via useLongPress, which swallows the following tap) while TagChipRow/AdaptiveTagRow stay store-free and emit tag-long-press; settingsStore.muteTag trims, is idempotent, no-ops when logged out, persists through setMuteTags and drives a 2 s App.vue snackbar whose wording comes from the disk-write result; /mute-tags lists settings.mutedTags() synchronously with a leading removal button.
The muted-tag set belongs to the account-level backup domain: backupAccountKeys(uid) returns the R18/R18G, AI-mode and mute_tags keys, while mute_tags is deliberately absent from BACKUP_DEVICE_KEYS.

AI-'only' and tag-mute data-layer removal is funnelled through two composables — useTagMuteVisible(useAiOnlyVisible(items)) in IllustList, NovelList, Following, UserHome and Bookmarks — while the discover page composes isRestricted/shouldHideByAi/isTagMuted inline; search result rows are removed at the data layer and deliberately kept out of isRowMasked, and watch-later snapshots are exempt because they carry no tag data.

Watch later is a purely local staging list under the account-scoped key watch_later_${uid}: ordered snapshot entries {kind,id,title,coverUrl,userId,userName,addedAt} built from already-loaded page data, (WorkKind,id) dedupe, newest-first prepending, a 500-entry cap that drops the oldest with a module-prefixed warning, tolerant parsing that skips non-conforming entries, a zero-network list page with no pagination and no restriction overlay, and account-switch re-hydration guarded by a hydrateGeneration counter.

The watchlist surface is the server-side novel-series follow list, physically separate from watch later: masked series render mask_text read-only with no action, cancel-follow goes through a confirmation layer plus createWatchlistToggle, the module-level store holds a cross-entry reactive series watch-state cache and a session-only 'not now' dismissal set, and /watchlist paginates through createWatchlistFeed.

Global search is entered from the radial FAB and from tag-chip taps that prefill and auto-run the query (there is no /search route); the sheet ignores IME composition events and re-runs an existing keyword on filter edits after a separate 450 ms debounce (FILTER_DEBOUNCE_MS), in addition to the 300 ms input debounce.

RankingEntryCard is rendered on IllustList's recommend sub-tab rather than on the discover page, is gated by the device-level ranking_entry setting, is fixed to today's daily ranking, collapses for the session and restores on refresh/remount, and navigates to /ranking while mode and date state stay on the ranking page.
The ranking page has no calendar picker: date navigation is arrow stepping clamped at today, and an explicit today value is normalized to null so it shares the today cache key with the default query.
